chunks: Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said:

A man's tongue was restrained among the people of al-Madinah during the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, in the illness in which he died. The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, entered upon him and said to him, 'Say: There is no god but Allah,' but he was unable to do so. The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, repeated it to him, but he was unable to do so. At the head of the man was a woman, so he said to her, 'Does this man have a mother?' She said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, I am his mother.' He said to her, 'Are you pleased with him or not?' She said, 'No, rather I am displeased.' The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said to her, 'Indeed, I would love that you become pleased with him.' She said, 'I am now pleased with him for your pleasure, O Messenger of Allah.' So he said to him, 'Say: There is no god but Allah.' He said, 'There is no god but Allah.'

He then said, 'Say: O He who accepts the little and pardons the much, accept from me the little and pardon from me the much; surely You are the Pardoning, the Forgiving.' So he said it. Then he said to him, 'What do you see?' He said, 'I see two black ones who have come upon me.' He said, 'Repeat it.' So he repeated it. Then he said, 'What do you see?' He said, 'They have moved away from me, and two white ones have entered, and the two black ones have departed. I no longer see them, and the two white ones have now drawn near to me to take my soul.' So he died that very hour.

key_terms.الْعَفُوُّ: the One who pardons and effaces sins
key_terms.بِنَفْسِي: with my soul, meaning to take my soul
key_terms.سَاخِطَةٌ: displeased or angry, referring here to the mother's state toward her son
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: the declaration of tawhid uttered at death

ai.seo_question: How does a mother's displeasure affect a person at the time of death in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a dying man who could not utter the shahadah until his mother became pleased with him, showing the grave spiritual effect of a parent's displeasure. It also teaches a du'a of seeking divine pardon and depicts signs at death, linking repentance, family rights, and one's final state.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.347 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said: "During the time of the Messenger of Allah (sw), a man from the people of Medina was unable to speak due to throes of death. The Messenger of Allah (sw) entered upon him and said:
'Say: There is no god but Allah (swt).' But the man was unable to say it.
The Messenger of Allah (sw) repeated it to him, but he still could not say it.
At the head of this man was a woman, and He asked her: 'Is this man’s mother present?'"
She said: 'Yes, O’ Messenger of Allah (sw), I am his mother.'
He asked her: 'Are you pleased with him or displeased?'
She said: 'I am displeased with him.'
The Messenger of Allah (sw) said to her: "I would like that you become pleased with him,"
She said: 'I am pleased with him for your sake, O’ Messenger of Allah (sw).'
He (sw) then said to him: "Say: There is no god but Allah (swt).'"
(the man) replied: "There is no god but Allah (swt)."

Then He (sw) said: 'Say: O’ One who accepts the small and forgives the great, accept from me the small and forgive the great, for You are the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.'
(the man) said it, and then He asked him, 'What do you see?'
(the man) replied: 'I see two dark figures approaching me.'
He (sw) said: 'Repeat the supplication.'
So he repeated it, and He (sw) said: 'What do you see now?'
(the man) replied: 'They have moved away from me, and two white figures have come in, and the dark figures have left. I no longer see them, and the white figures are now drawing close to me to take my soul.' The man then passed away thereafter.
